title: ER, OR, or AR?
kidRule: The 'er' sound at the end of a word is usually spelled E-R, especially for a person who does something, like REPORTER. Some words use O-R instead (often after the letter T, like CONDUCTOR) and a few use A-R, and those have to be remembered.
hint: Listen to the 'er' sound at the end. That sound has more than one spelling! Picture the word in your mind: which ending looks right?
reminder: The 'er' ending has three spellings: E-R, O-R, and A-R. If your first try did not work, try another one!

check.question: Why does REPORTER end with E-R?
check.correctAnswer: Because E-R is the most common way to spell the 'er' ending, especially for a person who does something!
distractors: Because O-R is only used for animals
Because long words must always end with E-R

words.def: A person who finds out the news and tells it or writes it for everyone.
words.sent: The reporter asked the mayor three questions.
words.story: A young reporter named Nellie Bly raced around the world in just 72 days in 1889 and 1890, and wrote about the whole trip for her newspaper!
words.card: The parrot *reporter* squawked the news from the *port*: the pirates are out of crackers!

words.def: A person who leads a group of musicians, or who looks after the riders on a train.
words.sent: The conductor waved her baton and the music began.
words.story: A conductor usually leads the musicians with a thin stick called a baton!
words.card: The *conductor* fixed his baton with *duct* tape!

words.def: A person who pretends to be someone else in a play, movie, or show.
words.sent: The actor wore a pirate costume on stage.
words.story: In ancient Greece, an actor wore a big mask so that even people in the back rows could tell which character he was playing!
words.card: 'Watch me *act* like a potato,' said the world's silliest *actor*!

words.def: Money used in the United States and some other countries, worth 100 cents.
words.sent: I found a dollar under the couch cushion.
words.story: A dollar bill is not made of paper! It is mostly cotton with some linen, which is why it can survive the washing machine.
words.card: My *doll* paid one *dollar* for a ride on the cat!

words.def: Someone who comes to see a person or a place for a while.
words.sent: A visitor from Japan came to our school.
words.story: Millions of visitors go to the Louvre museum in Paris every year, more than any other art museum in the world!
words.card: The *visitor* tried to *sit* on a chair made of jelly!

words.def: A person whose job is to know the rules of a country and help people with them.
words.sent: The lawyer explained the rules to the family.
words.story: Before he became president, Abraham Lincoln worked as a lawyer in Illinois!
words.card: The owl *lawyer* said there is no *law* against hooting at noon!

words.def: The part of a shirt that goes around your neck, or a band around a pet's neck.
words.sent: My dog has a red collar with a little bell.
words.story: Pet collars are very old: a dog collar found in an ancient Egyptian tomb even had the dog's name written on it!
words.card: The puppy spilled *col*a all over his shiny new *collar*!

words.def: A person riding in a car, bus, train, boat, or plane who is not the driver.
words.sent: Each passenger found a seat on the bus.
words.story: The biggest passenger planes can carry more than 500 people at once!
words.card: Please *pass* the peanuts to the elephant *passenger* in seat nine!

words.def: A teacher at a college or university.
words.sent: The professor showed us a rock from the moon.
words.story: The scientist Marie Curie was the first woman to become a professor at the famous University of Paris!
words.card: The *professor* is a *pro* at juggling chalk!

words.def: A chart that shows the days, weeks, and months of the year.
words.sent: I circled my birthday on the calendar.
words.story: Our calendar adds an extra day, February 29, about every four years, because Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days to go around the sun!
words.card: At the *end* of the *calendar*, the months threw a party for December!
